newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras hikes phone prices to woo partner.
newsitem.headline: Honduras hikes phone prices to woo partner.

text.p: Honduran state telephone company Hondutel on Wednesday said it would raise prices for local service by 35 percent to try and entice a foreign partner.
"The increase in tariffs improves the financial situation of the company, which will help us to better negotiate with a foreign partner," Hondutel head Ramon Morales told reporters.
He said the increase would take effect on Thursday and would coincide with a drop of more than 50 percent in international telephone charges, excluding calls to the United States and Central America.
The local tariff increases should raise Hondutel's revenues by some 21 percent, company officials said.
The government is seeking to sell 45 percent of the phone company by the end of the year. It needs to raise about $1 billion to raise service to international standards.
There are currently 195,000 telephone lines for the country's 5.9 million citizens, or a ratio of 3.5 phones for each 100 citizens, compared to 17 per 100 in nearby Costa Rica.
